items.title: Where Is the Silver?
items.task: Walk the pavilion. Find the silver.
items.reveal: There is no silver skin. The name came later, as a pair with the Golden Pavilion.
items.notes: Let them search before the reveal.

items.title: Gold vs Silver
items.task: Which feels richer: gold leaf in the sun, or this quieter garden?
items.reveal: There is no right answer. Japanese gardens often prize restraint. Do not turn that into a slogan.

items.title: The Shogun Who Preferred Beauty
items.hook: A shogun who lost a war still shaped how Kyoto looks at beauty.

moreInfo.title: Higashiyama
moreInfo.text: Ashikaga Yoshimasa lived here in retreat. Tea, gardens and quiet rooms grew around him. He was not a cartoon of peace. Confirm names and dates before live.
moreInfo.audioText: Ashikaga Yoshimasa was a shogun who lost control of a war and still left Kyoto a taste for quiet rooms, tea and gardens. Call that Higashiyama culture if you like. Do not make him a simple saint. We will check the history before this is live.

items.reveal: Beauty here is a leftover of power, not a replacement for it.
items.notes: Confirm Higashiyama / Yoshimasa biography. Avoid caricature.
